- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 2–5%.
- If sentiment is neutral or negative (≤0.33), model often underestimates; adjust downward bias by +1–3% to align with true mean reversion.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > +5% above recent high), model frequently overcorrects downward; cap subsequent forecast drops at 30% of prior peak.
- Model underestimates mean reversion in 30-day horizon when sentiment is flat; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to account for lagged momentum.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often fails to catch the reversal; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% at the 15-day mark.
- Forecast errors are more pronounced in early horizon (1–7 days) when sentiment is volatile; apply smoothing filter to reduce early overshoots.
